title: M-L-Ch

segments.voice: Yesterday, A-V-D: avodah, the work of the soil, the bondage in Egypt, the service of the heart. Your line was work is worship. Who was your one task really for? Today, the question behind every service: who's in charge? Day one thousand three hundred seventy-seven.

The elders of Israel walk to Ramah, to the prophet Samuel, who is old now, and they put a request in front of him. In the King James: "now make us a king to judge us like all the nations." Like everyone else. A palace, a crown, someone to lead the army out. The text says plainly how Samuel took it: "But the thing displeased Samuel." He goes to pray about it, and the answer he gets cuts two ways. That answer, and the Hebrew word for king inside it, is where today begins.
screen: `THE ELDERS COME TO SAMUEL.` → `MAKE US A KING.` → `THE THING DISPLEASED SAMUEL.`

segments.voice: M-L-Ch. Mem, lamed, chaf. Melech, a king. Malchut, kingship, a kingdom. And the verb, to reign. Turn it four ways. First, the answer Samuel gets. God tells him to listen to the people, and then: "they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them." Reign is this root. A human throne is granted, but with a long warning about what kings take: sons, daughters, fields, harvests. Kingship in the Bible starts with that tension already built in. Second, a song sung long before any of that. On the far shore of the sea, after the crossing, Moses and the people sing, and the song ends: "The LORD shall reign for ever and ever." The people have no king of their own yet, and they sing that. Third, the blessings. The standard blessing names God melech ha-olam, king of the world, so the word comes up over bread, over wine, over a new fruit. Fourth, the kingdom as something you accept. The Mishnah, in tractate Berakhot, asks why the Shema's first paragraph is read before the next one. Its answer: so that a person first takes on the yoke of the kingdom of heaven, ol malchut shamayim, and only then the yoke of the commandments. Kingship, in that picture, isn't seized or imposed. It's accepted, by the one saying the words, morning and evening. Which leaves the root asking a plain question: who, or what, rules here?
screen: `THEY HAVE REJECTED ME.` · `THE LORD SHALL REIGN FOR EVER.` · `MELECH HA-OLAM: KING OF THE WORLD.` · `THE YOKE OF THE KINGDOM, ACCEPTED.` · then, large: `מֶלֶךְ · מַלְכוּת`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: ask what rules your day. Settle, and breathe. Look back over the last few hours. What's been sitting on the throne? Maybe your phone. Maybe a deadline, a worry, a grudge, someone's opinion of you. Name it, plainly, without scolding yourself. Then ask the second question: what would you want ruling instead? Kindness, a promise, a value, God, your own best judgment. Let that one sit on the throne for the rest of this quiet. If you pray, you can say the Shema, the way the Mishnah describes taking on the kingdom. The bell holds the time.
M-L-Ch. Mem, lamed, chaf: melech, a king; malchut, kingship; the reign the elders asked for and the one sung at the sea. Today's word.
Your line: kingship. Today, once, when you feel something pushing you around, stop and ask: did I crown this? Day one thousand three hundred seventy-seven.

howItsDone: Jews say the Shema morning and evening, which the Mishnah calls accepting the yoke of the kingdom of heaven, and the standard blessing names God melech ha-olam, king of the world; on Rosh Hashanah a section of the service, Malchuyot, is devoted to God's kingship.

what it means: melech is king and malchut is kingship: who rules, and who is accepted as ruling.

notes: Quotations from the KJV; confirm the Judaism path accepts KJV here.
1 Samuel 8:1 says Samuel was old, 8:4 places the elders at Ramah; 8:11–17 lists what a king will take. Paraphrased.
'The people have no king of their own yet' at the Song of the Sea is a reading of the narrative order; confirm framing.
Mishnah Berakhot 2:2 (Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah) paraphrased: first the yoke of the kingdom of heaven, then the yoke of the commandments.
'The standard blessing names God melech ha-olam' avoids an every-blessing claim. Day 1355 already taught baruch atah; this day mentions the formula only briefly.
howItsDone names Malchuyot in the Rosh Hashanah musaf; confirm.
